newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia PM rules out Chechnya secession.
newsitem.headline: Russia PM rules out Chechnya secession.

text.p: Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on Monday ruled out any prospect of Chechnya being allowed to secede from the Russian Federation but he said Moscow wanted a peaceful solution to the 21-month war there.
"Russia's territorial integrity is not up for discussion," Itar-Tass news agency quoted Chernomyrdin as saying as he presented new security chief Ivan Rybkin to members of the Security Council.
"We do not need war. We will hold negotiations and move further in that direction," Interfax news agency quoted him as saying.

Rybkin replaced the explosive Alexander Lebed, who was sacked last Thursday for making too many waves in the Kremlin. Lebed put together an August 31 peace deal with separatist leaders which ended the fighting.

"Ahead of us lies some very careful work -- we can't just go charging in," said Chernomyrdin. "We think there should be understanding for all sides, including the Chechens. There will be understanding and there will be a solution."

Critics rounded on Lebed for signing the peace deal, which said Russian troops would be gradually withdrawn from the rebel territory and postponed discussions on Chechnya's future status for five years.
There was no immediate reaction to Chernomyrdin's comments from the Chechens, who cautiously welcomed earlier statements from Kremlin officials that there would be no return to war.
